problem: Current VLN methods struggle to navigate efficiently to small objects in unseen household environments because small objects occupy few pixels and are frequently occluded.
motivation: Household service robots must follow high-level natural language instructions and find small objects such as those in ALFRED tasks. Small objects are typically stored in or on containers, so common-sense object-container relations can guide exploration and cut wasted search.
key_idea: Use prior object-container knowledge in a two-stage navigation policy with Exploration Memory: first navigate to likely containers via their semantic masks, then switch to the small object's semantic mask once it is found.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that replacing direct small-object search with container-guided search reduces unnecessary exploration and improves navigation efficiency on ALFRED.
method: Prior object-container knowledge: uses relationships between small objects and their likely containers to guide the search.
Two-stage navigation policy: stage 1 heads toward relevant containers using semantic masks; stage 2 switches to the small object's semantic mask once the object is detected.
Exploration Memory: stores explored regions to avoid redundant exploration and improve efficiency.
results: The abstract states only that experiments on the ALFRED benchmark show prior knowledge improves navigation efficiency. No numbers or baselines are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results and details are unknown.
Relies on hand-specified or prior object-container relations, which may not generalize to unusual object placements.
